title: 2026 Sedona Mountain Bike Festival: Finally Fall – Spencer Harding
content:
Spencer rolled upstate this past weekend for the first Fall iteration of the Sedona Mountain Bike Festival in…well, Sedona! This was the event’s first Fall seasonal festival, a switch from Spring after many years of unfortunate weather. The weather was perfect, and Spencer found some sweet brands and bits to highlight. See what he found below…

Sedona Mountain Bike Festival

The Sedona Mountain Bike Festival feels more like the bike-demo portion of the now-defunct Interbike than a larger trade show like Sea Otter. The experience really does cater to allowing attendees to ride bikes, try on clothes, and put their hands on products they have seen on the internet. It is a very tactile experience, and as such, I have a whole separate post focusing on actually riding some bikes instead of just shooting pretty photos of them.

Fear not, I also have a whole section in this article focusing on some beautiful builds from the festival.

From Spring to Fall

In the past, Sedona Mountain Bike Festival was hosted in the spring. After a few years of snow and rain that made riding difficult or nearly impossible, the festival owners moved the event to the Fall. With spring peppered with bike and gear releases ahead of Sea Otter, many companies kept their releases close to their chest before the big trade show.

Free from the clutches of product release cycles, Sedona MTB Fest feels like it can stand on its own legs and focus on what it does best: get people out riding in a gorgeous place. The festival offers group rides, shuttles all over Sedona, clinics, classes, and any other permutation you can imagine to give people an excuse to get out of the festival grounds and onto some red dirt.

After the initial 9 am “Running of the Dads” to get in line for precious demo slots, the festival calms down for a few hours. It is a very hurry-up-and-wait situation for all the brave souls managing the bike fleets. I have only ever seen such a line of eager riders forming well before opening at one festival, Sedona.

Twisted Spoke CBD

My curiosity was initially caught by Twisted Spoke’s CBD chamois cream offering, which seems as novel as it could be useful. I was really in the market for some sleepy time supplements and snagged a jar of CBN softgels to replace my usual THC and CBN gummies. Gabe had a plethora of gummies, tinctures, and even sparkling waters with more permutations of acronyms than one could imagine. I’m looking forward to sleeping well with these tablets after the festival.

Adidas 5.10

Adidas is finally leaning into fully rebadging the 5.10 lineup with the triple stripes. As seen above, they have the new Slueth Pro, Freerider Pro Boa, and Freerider Clip coming at various times in 2027.

Also, the much-lauded Guide Tennie is back!

Rogue Panda

The Pandas have been busy up in Flagstaff this past year. With the latest release of their new Double Track mounting system, Rogue Panda once again shows their dedication to constantly pushing bag technology forward. The Double Track system uses two carbon poles and TPU spacers for a more secure and robust mounting system for their custom frame bags. They also had their two new rack-top bags: the Elden rack-top harness and Picket Post. The rear rack also showcased their Buckskin mini panniers, which use the Old Man Mountain Flip mounting system. Add in their redesigned Blue Ridge Handlebar Harness V2 and Rogue Panda has every bag you could need for your dream setup in all kinds of amazing fabrics, patterns, and colors.

Velo In A Jar

Ava of Velo in a Jar had a humble booth, featuring recycled jewelry made from bike tubes, beer cans, and even clock parts. She had a menagerie of great gifts. Her work offered a cozy respite from the downhill bro aesthetic of many booths.

Cognative MTB

I love a snap-button shirt, so the Cognative MTB technical flannel caught my eye. With plenty of thoughtful details and technical fabrics that didn’t feel overly plasticky, the flannel felt nice in hand. You really can’t beat grabbing a fistful of shirts and ripping open snap buttons to air out on a long climb.

All Over Apparel

Salida-based All Over had a small but lovely lineup of clothes on show at the fest. With the main focus and name seemingly a play on overalls, All Over offers a technical stretch-fabric iteration of the classic. While the overalls look quite fun, it is almost always too hot for such fashion in Tucson, so I opted to snag a waffle tee that was oh so soooooft.

Rackspotting at Sedona MTB Fest

Rackspotting at Sedona MTB Fest wasn’t nearly the whole gallery level as the rackspotting at MADE. I found a few gems hidden between all the Stumpjumpers and Trail Cats, including one of the gnarliest derailleurs I’ve ever seen that probably still works…

High Country Adaptive Sports

While out on a test ride, I was lucky enough to catch a group of riders seated in Bowhead adaptive mountain bikes alongside some guides from High Country Adaptive Sports. They offer year-round adaptive programming and recreation opportunities across the Arizona high country.

Beautiful Bicycles of Sedona MTB Fest

I was able to fish out a few beautiful builds from the stalls at the festival. While many companies solely had demo bikes, a few brands- well, just Reeb and Revel- had some gorgeous bikes that warranted a closer look, Radavist style.

Reeb SST Prototype

Reeb showed an updated version of their short-travel steel full-suspension bike, the SST, at the Sedona MTB Festival. While the details weren’t official yet, a few leaked out. Adjusting for yearly geometry inflation, the new SST will have a slightly slacker headtube and a slightly steeper seat tube, around .5º, I was told, for both. The new SST will also feature a butted top tube instead of straight gauge. The bearing will now be removable via collet to make service easier for the home mechanics. The SST will feature revised kinematics, though I don’t have more detail than that. Saving the best for last, 10 mm more stack height across sizes, hell yeah. This bike looks sweeter than ever, and all the improvements make this bike a banger.

Devon’s Custom Reeb Dirt Jumper

Devon is the marketing manager over at I9, and when he helped Reeb out with many days of unpaid labor to help them with bike demos over the past few years, they decided to repay him with this sweet custom Dirt Jumper. Don’t be fooled; Devon is a tall glass of water, and this custom geo was definitely a necessity for someone of his stature. The DJ is dripping in gold I9 bits and topped off with some sparkly labeled Schwable tires, oooohweeeeee.

Revel El Grande Jefe

Revel recently announced their foray into the 32er world with their updated El Jefe titanium hardtail, aptly named El Grande Jefe. With one of the more elegant seat tube bends and a helluva head tube, this hardtail was looking amazing at the show. While this was a rideable prototype, I’m saving myself for a proper ride when production forks become available in the next few months; stay tuned for a full review of the El Grande Jefe soon…

Revel Ti Ranger

Whooooooweee, was this thing a looker. The Ti Ranger was announced just recently, and the initial run of 10 frames sold out in 2 hours. What was expected to just be a fun side project has really caught people’s attention. The combination of a metal, especially titanium, front triangle and Revel’s highly regarded CBF carbon rear triangle is truly stunning. Pulling from all of Revel’s expertise in carbon and titanium, the Ti Ranger is a perfect showpiece to completely encapsulate the brand. Unlike the El Grande Jefe, I did take this for a quick spin; see my Speed Dating article today on the site for some ride details.

Wrap Up

Ok there was a quick downpour on the day at the festival, so it wasn’t perfect weather, but that storm did present a double rainbow afterward with minimal wetting of the trails. I had as lovely a time strolling the aisles as I did getting out on the trails right by the festival grounds and farther around Sedona. With trails available right out of the gate, you couldn’t ask for a more beautiful and apt place to ride a mountain bike than Sedona. I’m already looking forward to 2027…

Please check out my speed-dating bike demos article for a few quick first-ride reviews from the festival!
